what: Kimberly-Clark makes everyday paper and hygiene products: Huggies nappies, Kleenex tissues, Cottonelle and Andrex toilet paper, Kotex and Depend. It has sold a majority stake in its international tissue business to focus on branded personal care.
customers: Consumers worldwide through supermarkets, pharmacies and e-commerce, plus institutional buyers.
money: nappies, feminine care and adult incontinence products
washroom and wiping products for offices and factories
moat: Brands people buy by habit in categories where quality failures are unacceptable, with shelf space and scale in pulp buying.
risks: Sales have fallen for three years as volumes declined after price increases
Birth rates are falling in its main nappy markets
Own-label products take share in a weak economy
Pulp and energy costs move margins
opportunities: Reshaping the portfolio around higher-margin branded personal care
A dividend yield near 5% raised for more than five decades
Cost savings programmes have protected margins through weak volumes
watch: Organic volume growth, which has been the weak point, rather than price.
